examples.question_text:
A loan of $\$24\,000$ charges $12\%$ p.a., compounded monthly. Repayments of $\$1000$ are made at the end of each month.
(a) Derive the balance expression from a geometric series and use logarithms to find the number of monthly repayments required.
(b) Find the smaller final repayment, to the nearest cent.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The monthly interest rate is $r=0.12/12=0.01$. The first month's interest is $24\,000(0.01)=\$240$, which is less than the repayment.
Let $A_n$ be the balance immediately after $n$ repayments.
$\begin{align*} A_0&=24\,000\\ A_1&=24\,000(1.01)-1000\\ A_2&=24\,000(1.01)^2-1000(1.01)-1000\\ A_n&=24\,000(1.01)^n-1000(1.01)^{n-1}-\cdots-1000 \end{align*}$
The repayment terms form a geometric series with first term $1000$, common ratio $1.01$ and $n$ terms.
$A_n=24\,000(1.01)^n-1000\left[\dfrac{(1.01)^n-1}{0.01}\right]$
Set the balance to zero.
$\begin{align*} 0&=24\,000(1.01)^n-1000\left[\dfrac{(1.01)^n-1}{0.01}\right]\\ 0&=240(1.01)^n-1000(1.01)^n+1000\\ 760(1.01)^n&=1000\\ (1.01)^n&=\dfrac{25}{19}\\ n&=\dfrac{\log(25/19)}{\log1.01}\\ n&=27.580675\ldots \end{align*}$
There are $27$ full repayments and a smaller final repayment in month $28$.
(b) Calculate the balance after the $27$th full repayment.
$\begin{align*} A_{27}&=24\,000(1.01)^{27}-1000\left[\dfrac{(1.01)^{27}-1}{0.01}\right]\\ A_{27}&=576.125263\ldots \end{align*}$
The remaining balance earns one more month's interest before the final repayment. Using the unrounded balance, the final repayment is $A_{27}(1.01)=\$581.89$, to the nearest cent.

examples.question_text:
A borrower owes $\$16\,000$ on a loan charging $12\%$ p.a., compounded monthly. Repayments are made at the end of each month.
Explain whether the loan will ever be repaid if the monthly repayment is:
(a) $\$150$
(b) $\$160$.
examples.solution_text:
The first month's interest is $16\,000(0.12/12)=\$160$.
(a) The $\$150$ repayment does not cover the interest.
$A_1=16\,000(1.01)-150=16\,010$
The balance increases, so subsequent interest charges increase. The loan will never be repaid.
(b) The $\$160$ repayment covers the interest exactly.
$A_1=16\,000(1.01)-160=16\,000$
The balance remains $\$16\,000$ each month. No principal is repaid, so the loan will never be repaid.

examples.question_text:
A mortgage of $\$90\,000$ charges $6\%$ p.a., compounded monthly. Its contract allows $120$ months for repayment.
The borrower makes repayments of $\$1200$ at the end of each month. Use a geometric series and logarithms to find how many months before the contractual deadline the loan is paid off.
examples.solution_text:
The monthly rate is $r=0.06/12=0.005$. The repayment exceeds the first month's interest of $90\,000(0.005)=\$450$.
Let $A_n$ be the balance after $n$ repayments.
$\begin{align*} A_1&=90\,000(1.005)-1200\\ A_2&=90\,000(1.005)^2-1200(1.005)-1200\\ A_n&=90\,000(1.005)^n-1200(1.005)^{n-1}-\cdots-1200 \end{align*}$
The repayment terms form a geometric series with first term $1200$, common ratio $1.005$ and $n$ terms.
$A_n=90\,000(1.005)^n-1200\left[\dfrac{(1.005)^n-1}{0.005}\right]$
Set the balance to zero.
$\begin{align*} 0&=90\,000(1.005)^n-1200\left[\dfrac{(1.005)^n-1}{0.005}\right]\\ 0&=450(1.005)^n-1200(1.005)^n+1200\\ 750(1.005)^n&=1200\\ (1.005)^n&=1.6\\ n&=\dfrac{\log1.6}{\log1.005}\\ n&=94.235532\ldots \end{align*}$
The loan is cleared in month $95$, with a smaller final repayment.
It is paid off $120-95=25$ months before the deadline.
